sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2014. ADAMAWA (lecture handout, JGU Mainz, 4 Feb 2014). 26 pp.
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent and 'Jalaa': zero hits. Adamawa classification handout only.
No references at all listed for Komta (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); links only to Wikipedia and Wikidata Q60787676.

sources.note: Lists only Kleinewillinghöfer 2001 as reference; Jalaa AES 'extinct'; no Komta.
Bibliographic only: instance of language, country Nigeria, Glottolog komt1237; imported from en.wikipedia.

sources.citation: Adelberger, Jörg & Roger Blench. 2026. The peopling of the Muri Mountains, Northern Nigeria: evidence from linguistics and ethnography. Afrikanistik-Aegyptologie-Online. doi:10.18716/OJS/AAEO/2026_12031. 47 pp.
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent: zero hits; Kaltungo/Tangale appear only in migration narratives (e.g. 'Tangale people who camped for a while at Kaltungo'). Ethnohistorical synthesis, no phonology; Komta absent even from the population stratigraphy.

sources.note: Might carry a one-line entry for Komta under extinct/unclassified languages of Gombe State (location, status, source), which would settle whether any further data exist; will not contain phonology.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2014. African language isolates. Circulation draft, 30 June 2014, Cambridge. 49 pp. (Internet Archive copy of rogerblench.info/Language/Africa/General/African language)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent: zero hits. The Jalaa section 3.2.3 (pp. 9-10) says of Jalaa 'Three level tones are transcribed, as well as a falling tone'; nothing on stress; Komta is not mentioned anywhere in the draft.

sources.citation: Wikipedia. 'Komta language' (raw wikitext, rev. current 2026-09-17), quoting Kleinewillinghöfer 2010 ms.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Secondary: reports the ten alleged numerals and Kleinewillinghöfer's statement that 'The Komta people were dispelled and/or eradicated by the Tangale upon their arrival in the area around Kaltungo Peak'; 'extinct = early 20th century?'.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2010. Jalaa, the last member of an extinct language family. Ms., Workshop 'Language Isolates in Africa', Lyon, December 2010.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, not open: the recorded link leads to a login, a search-only view or a restricted repository; the linked copy is not accessible
sources.note: The sole document containing any Komta material (ten alleged numerals recalled second-hand in 2003). Worth opening only to confirm there is no phonological remark; by its own description the data are a scribbled list with no transcription conventions, so it cannot yield a stress statement.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. Atlas of Nigerian Languages (ed. III / IV), rogerblench.info.
sources.note: Could not be opened: rogerblench.info answers every request with an sgcaptcha redirect (HTTP 202 HTML), and the Internet Archive was 'Temporarily Offline' for the remainder of the session so no archived copy at the Internet Archive could be pulled. Unknown whether it carries a Komta entry; even if it does, an atlas entry would give location/status, not phonology.
